愁.meaning: Every <part>autumn</part>, a scarecrow watches the leaves fall and the birds fly south without him. His straw <part>heart</part> sinks a little lower with each one that leaves. By November he droops on his pole, buttons sagging: the picture of <kanji>distress</kanji>.
愁.on: One crow flies back to cheer him up and leaves him a tiny <sound>shoe</sound>.
愁.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' he moans, as a <sound>re</sound>d leaf lands on his nose.

汎.meaning: A chef makes one sauce for everything: <part>water drops</part>, salt and anything <part>commonplace</part> from the shelf. It goes on soup, cake, toast, even the cat's dinner. Never great, never bad, always there: her <kanji>general</kanji> sauce.
汎.on: One day she stirs in a spoon of <sound>hon</sound>ey and it's great on everything.
汎.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!' she sings, tipping a pot into the stream, and the sauce floats away <sound>yo</sound>nder: to drift.

遷.meaning: A zoo moves its reptile house <part>west</part>. A <part>large</part> basket with a <part>cobra</part> inside rolls up a <part>ramp</part> onto a train, and at every stop the cobra pokes its head out at the new view: desert, then hills, then sea. One long, slow <kanji>transition</kanji>.
遷.on: At the new zoo, a <sound>sen</sound>try checks the cobra's ticket.
遷.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' says the cobra at the sea, then sneezes in the salty air: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

租.meaning: A guard on a bridge stops every cart of <part>grain</part> and takes one sack from the pile, and <part>moreover</part> one more sack for every layer stacked on top. The farmers grumble about it, but they pay the <kanji>tariff</kanji>.
租.on: He stacks the sacks into a lumpy <sound>so</sound>fa and naps on it.

郡.meaning: A <part>mister</part> in a top hat rides round the edge of the land, planting a <part>pennant</part> on every hill he passes. When he gets back to where he started, every village inside the ring of flags shares one sheriff, one fair and one map: a new <kanji>county</kanji>.
郡.on: Big <sound>Gun</sound>ther wins the sheriff's job by carrying all the flags at once.
郡.kun: Along the river bank, he marks the county line with <sound>co</sound>ld <sound>ree</sound>ds.

勾.meaning: A yoga teacher tries to <part>wrap</part> her arm round her own back, bending her <part>elbow</part> further and further until she's tied in a bow. Her students copy, and soon every arm in the room is hooked and twisted. Today's lesson: how to <kanji>be bent</kanji>.
勾.on: Afterwards nobody can straighten up enough to lick an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
勾.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm flock of <sound>gee</sound>se waddles in and untangles them with their curved necks: a hook.

阜.meaning: A <part>snowman</part> in a flat park wants a view. <part>Ten</part> pigeons take pity on him and each bring one beakful of earth a day. By spring he stands, a bit melted but very proud, on top of a little <kanji>mound</kanji>.
阜.on: He keeps warm with a rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton for a scarf.

曹.meaning: Two clerks set up shop by the road with <part>one</part> plank laid across a <part>pole</part> at each end, right under the blazing <part>sun</part>. A rubber stamp, an inkpad and a sign: 'Back in five minutes'. Not much, but it's an <kanji>office</kanji>.
曹.on: They scrub the ink off their hands with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap from the stream.

佳.meaning: A mole hangs his tiny hat on a <part>coat hook</part> by his door and shows off his new home: a <part>double mound</part>, one hill of soil neatly piled on another, with a balcony. The other moles gasp. A two-storey molehill is <kanji>excellent</kanji>.
佳.on: His neighbour, a big orange <sound>ca</sound>rp, pops up from the pond to applaud.

藤.meaning: A <part>bodybuilder</part> trains on the <part>grass</part> under the <part>moon</part>, lifting weights beneath a vine that drapes long purple flower bunches over his bench. Every rep shakes loose a shower of petals. His favourite gym is under the <kanji>wisteria</kanji>.
藤.on: One petal lands on his big <sound>toe</sound> and he squeaks.
藤.kun: He naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton there, then drives home in his <sound>jee</sound>p, petals in his hair.

葛.meaning: A gardener puts up a <part>sunshade</part> over a patch of <part>grass</part> and goes in for lunch. When she comes back, a twisting vine has climbed the shade, swallowed it whole and is reaching for her chair. She digs it out and finds a fat, starchy white root: <kanji>arrowroot</kanji>.
葛.on: She grinds the root to flour and fries a crispy <sound>katsu</sound> in it.
葛.kun: Her <sound>coo</sound>k squeezes yu<sound>zu</sound> over the top and serves it on the vine.

嫉.meaning: A <part>woman</part> knits her cat a sweater, but the cat runs off <part>rapidly</part> next door every time the neighbour opens a tin of tuna. She glares over the fence, needles clacking, green to the ears. She's <kanji>jealous</kanji> of a tin of fish.
嫉.on: She spies on them from behind a flapping bed <sound>sheet</sound> on the line.
嫉.kun: Next she knits it a <sound>so</sound>ck and a <sound>ne</sound>t hat, and the cat wears both next door.

諭.meaning: A tiny alien parks its <part>spaceship</part> on a farmer's roof. She climbs up and gives it a long, stern <part>speech</part> about gutters, parking and asking first. The alien droops its antennae, says sorry and moves to the field. A firm but fair <kanji>rebuke</kanji>.
諭.on: Then she softens and hands it a <sound>yu</sound>zu for the trip home.
諭.kun: The alien gives her a <sound>sa</sound>ri woven from moonlight and a <sound>to</sound>ffee to say sorry.

漸.meaning: <part>Water drops</part> fall from a warm, leaky tap onto a chocolate bunny, one at a time. No sudden <part>beheading</part> with a knife: the ears go first, then the head, drip by drip, all week. The bunny shrinks <kanji>steadily</kanji>.
漸.on: Its brown puddle trickles out into a raked <sound>zen</sound> garden.
漸.kun: A girl <sound>yo</sound>dels '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo!' when at last only the tail is left.

股.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> hiking all night under the <part>moon</part> keeps her map in a pocket strapped to her leg above the knee, so she can slap it out mid-stride. Her horse thinks she's patting it. Best place for a map: the <kanji>thigh</kanji>.
股.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala rides in the pocket on her other leg.
股.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma tucked a <sound>ta</sound>co in there for it too.

蓋.meaning: A picnicker sets a <part>dish</part> of jam tarts on the <part>grass</part>, turns round, and half are <part>gone</part>: wasps. She flips her sun hat over the rest and sits on it. Next time she'll bring a proper <kanji>cover</kanji>.
蓋.on: Her <sound>gui</sound>de dog lies across the hat to keep the wasps out.
蓋.kun: It even rests a <sound>foo</sound>t on her <sound>ta</sound>co box, like a lid.

某.meaning: Every night, someone hangs a <part>yoke</part> with two buckets of fresh milk on the <part>tree</part> at the crossroads, and nobody ever sees who. The villagers drink it and thank Mister Whatsit, You-Know-Who, or just <kanji>so-and-so</kanji>.
某.on: One night someone leaves a <sound>bou</sound>lder there instead, with a smiley face.
某.kun: Next, a <sound>so</sound>ck, <sound>re</sound>d and stuffed with <sound>ga</sound>rlic, hangs there for the <sound>shee</sound>p.

逝.meaning: Great-grandpa's last wish: <part>fold</part> his old letters into paper boats and set them on the <part>ramp</part> down to the river. One by one they slide into the water and drift off into the mist, as if waving goodbye for him. He has <kanji>departed</kanji>.
逝.on: In his old steel <sound>sa</sound>fe the family finds only more paper, for more boats.
逝.kun: A <sound>yu</sound>zu, his favourite fruit, floats after the boats.

薪.meaning: A village keeps a friendly dragon that eats only fresh <part>grass</part>: no hay, just <part>new</part> green stalks. Every morning it munches an armful and breathes fire into the bakery ovens. Grass in, flames out: the farmers are growing its <kanji>fuel</kanji>.
薪.on: A child sits by its warm belly to thaw one frozen <sound>shin</sound>.
薪.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma toasts a <sound>ki</sound>wi on its breath for a snack.

侯.meaning: A pompous noble hangs his velvet cloak on a <part>coat hook</part>, fixes his medals on with a <part>staple</part>, then throws a <part>dart</part> at a map to pick his next castle. He's not a king, not even a duke, but you must bow: he's a <kanji>marquis</kanji>.
侯.on: He eats his ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne with a knife and fork.

桁.meaning: Builders at a busy <part>crossroads</part> want one bridge over all four roads, so they chop the tallest <part>tree</part> in town and lay it from rooftop to rooftop. Cars pass under, cats stroll across the top. The whole junction leans on one <kanji>beam</kanji>.
桁.on: A cat walks the length of it with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in its mouth.
桁.kun: At lunch a builder boils a <sound>ke</sound>ttle and eats a <sound>ta</sound>co up there.

醸.meaning: A grandma keeps her homemade cider in an old <part>dynamite</part> crate hidden under the <part>laundry pile</part>, where it's warm and dark. It bubbles and fizzes and now and then pops its cork. All her shirts smell of apples. She has a strong <kanji>brew</kanji> going.
醸.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops out of the laundry, hiccupping.
醸.kun: '<sound>Ca</sound>lm down,' she tells it, and wipes the cider off its nose with a <sound>mo</sound>p.

膝.meaning: A fisherman sits under the <part>moon</part> with his back to a <part>tree</part> and an <part>umbrella</part> over his head against the <part>water</part> spraying off the lake. His cat curls up on the only dry spot left, the bend of his leg: his <kanji>knee</kanji>.
膝.on: When the rain gets worse he throws a bed <sound>sheet</sound> over them both.
膝.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>, hu<sound>zzah</sound>!' he cheers when a fish bites, and the cat doesn't budge.

捗.meaning: A diver who can't swim clips an <part>anchor</part> to her belt and goes for a <part>walk</part> along the seabed, one heavy step at a time, towards a sunken ship. Fish zip in rings around her, but every step counts: slow, steady <kanji>progress</kanji>.
捗.on: Her reward inside the wreck: a sealed tin of <sound>choc</sound>olate.
捗.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, staying <sound>ca</sound>lm as a <sound>do</sound>lphin tows her the last bit.

謎.meaning: An old owl leads hikers <part>astray</part> with one short <part>speech</part>: 'What has roots nobody sees and stands taller than trees?' They wander in circles thinking until dark, and only when they answer does the path appear. The owl lives on a <kanji>riddle</kanji>.
謎.on: The forest paths twist round its tree like a hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze.
謎.kun: The last hiker shares her <sound>na</sound>an with a lost <sound>zo</sound>mbie who's been stuck on it for years.

訟.meaning: A man slips on a banana peel in a <part>public</part> park, stands up and gives a furious <part>speech</part> to the crowd, pointing at the banana. Then he hires a lawyer and takes it to court. Nobody has ever tried to <kanji>sue</kanji> a fruit before.
訟.on: The trial becomes the best <sound>show</sound> in town.

穫.meaning: A <part>falconer</part> sends his hawk circling over the fields of <part>grain</part>, not to hunt but to scare off the crows. The farmers cut the golden stalks in peace while it wheels overhead. Not one ear stolen this year: the best <kanji>harvest</kanji> yet.
穫.on: The hawk's reward is a picked-clean chicken <sound>carc</sound>ass from the farm's soup pot.

勲.meaning: A firefighter has to <part>move</part> a whole bed of <part>hot coals</part> out of a burning bakery before the oven bursts, bucket by bucket, gloves smoking. She saves the bakery and its cat. The mayor pins on a medal cast from one of the coals, for <kanji>merit</kanji>.
勲.on: The cat she saved sleeps wrapped in her coat like a co<sound>coon</sound>.
勲.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals the cat at the thank-you <sound>su</sound>pper, as an <sound>o</sound>range rolls into its bowl.

嵐.meaning: A tickly cloud settles on a <part>mountain</part>'s nose, and the mountain sneezes. The <part>wind</part> rushes down its slopes, flattening tents, bending pines and sending hats and hailstones flying across the valley. Everyone in it is caught in the <kanji>storm</kanji>.
嵐.on: Below, the planes waiting on the <sound>run</sound>way rock on their wheels.
嵐.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' A hiker's bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men flies off and lands on a <sound>shee</sound>p.

陛.meaning: A ladybird climbs to the top of a heap of <part>soil</part>, plants a <part>pennant</part> made from a petal, and bangs <part>two spoons</part> together for silence. Every ant in the garden bows low: 'Yes, your <kanji>highness</kanji>.'
陛.on: Her throne is a single golden stalk of <sound>hay</sound>, held up by two ants.
